Task 3.2.4: Anomaly Detection – Multiple Metrics In Year 1, HPE conducted some preliminary work using Deep Neural Networks for multi-metric anomaly detection. This effort will be expanded upon in Year 2. HPE will work with NREL to determine if there are collection(s) of dependent or correlated metrics for which it makes sense to use multi-metric anomaly detection in order to, for instance, improve performance (reduce false positives) compared to single metric anomaly detection. NREL deliverables: • NREL to provide a subset of metrics (based on domain knowledge) for which it makes sense touse multi-metric anomaly detection. • NREL to work with HPE on proposing models of anomalies for metrics that correlate with eachother. This will be used to test anomaly detection pipelines in an unsupervised fashion. • NREL to help design tests to validate predictions of algorithms. HPE deliverables: • HPE to create a correlation engine to correlate various metrics and automatically identify metrics to use with multi-metric anomaly detection. • HPE to create multi-metric anomaly detection pipelines, based either on machine learning or deep learning. The results will be compared to those created using single metric algorithms Task 3.2.5: Real-time Streaming Analytics Real-time streaming analytics will be conducted on data from Eagle, and will focus on anomaly detection. In the context of this task, “real-time” refers to the use of metrics streamed to Kafka, and not to the relation between the occurrence of an event and its subsequent detection by the AIOps anomaly detection pipeline. HPE will work with NREL to identify key metrics of interest that should be focused on. NREL deliverables: • Use platform provided in Task 1 to host KM components. • NREL to identify high priority metrics for which it makes sense to do real-time anomaly detection. NREL to get all the key metrics onto Kafka. • If not otherwise available, NREL will create some manufactured events or data streams that HP can run the real-time anomaly detection algorithms against. Suggestions include unplugging on or more sensors (e.g., flow meters, temperature sensors, pressure sensors), changing a set-poinon a CDU, or changing a set-point on a Cooling Rack. • NREL to provide both data science feedback on the algorithms as well as operational effectiveness of the associated results of the real-time anomaly detection. 7 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. HPE deliverables: • HPE to create a python package for running anomaly detection engines in real-time. For some of the algorithms, there will be a separate package to re-compute models offline. Task 3.2.6: Real-time Automated Anomaly Detection Given the large number of metrics, and the large volumes of associated data, an automated anomaly detection pipeline is needed as manual manipulation of the metrics and data will be impractical and close to impossible. The anomaly detection pipeline will use either statistical anomaly detection models or Deep Neural Networks (DNNs).
